metadata.title: [Perf][V1][PP] Retain persistent request rows across empty steps
metadata.body:
Contributed by PLI Labs (Proprietary Legal Intelligence). Written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and reviewed in three rounds before opening.

**Depends on #1371.** The first commit of this branch is #1371; review only the second commit here. Stack order: #1371, then this PR.

**Credit.** This is a V1-runner port of the idea in #1263 by `Peuqui` (stop resending a request's token history to the V2 runner every decode step). The V1 retention code is ours; the approach is theirs.

## Purpose

Empty synchronous PP steps discard V1 persistent request rows and the scheduler's previous-step record. The next decode step then resends and rebuilds the complete token history. With VLLM_PP_KEEP_BATCH=1, retain rows and the matching record across fully empty steps, while removing finished and preempted requests. Nonempty steps keep the existing replacement behavior.

This PR is based on the companion **[Bugfix][V1][PP] Preserve synchronous speculative step ownership** (#1371); its first commit is that PR. Review that correctness change separately; this incremental change is opt-in. It is the V1 counterpart to #1263's existing V2 history reuse. SpeculativeConfig owns method capability, and SchedulerConfig owns the serialized retention setting. Explicit unsupported requests fail with the setting's name.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m tools.generate_architecture_reference --check
python -m tools.generate_env_reference --check
python tools/pre_commit/check_env_metadata.py
python tools/pre_commit/check_env_registration.py
python -m tools.config_inventory --check
python tools/pre_commit/check_layering.py
python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/tools tests/tools/test_architecture_reference.py tests/tools/test_architecture_doc_urls.py tests/tools/test_architecture_check_scope.py
python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/config tests/config/test_pp_keep_batch_policy.py tests/config/test_runtime_default_ownership.py
python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/v1 tests/v1/core/test_pp_keep_batch.py tests/v1/worker/test_pp_keep_batch_runner.py tests/v1/engine/test_pp_spec_decode_cadence.py tests/v1/core/test_pp_spec_decode_inflight.py tests/v1/worker/test_pp_spec_decode_history.py
```

For a public target/drafter pair already admitted by synchronous PP, set TARGET_CHECKPOINT and DRAFT_CHECKPOINT to those identifiers. Run the same command with ENABLED=0 and 1 in disabled/enabled/enabled/disabled order:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 VLLM_PP_KEEP_BATCH="$ENABLED" \
  vllm serve "$TARGET_CHECKPOINT" --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --max-num-seqs 4 --no-async-scheduling \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$DRAFT_CHECKPOINT\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":3}"
```

Warm greedy and seeded sampled paths. Compare complete token IDs and per-request histories with retention off/on for one request, staggered requests, one remaining request, cancellation, preemption and prefix-cache reset. Confirm that a fully empty step keeps only live nonpreempted rows and that the next step omits their history resend. Record first-token latency, decode-only milliseconds per verification round and acceptance separately. Repeat at longer contexts supported by the selected model. Test plain decode as well as speculation.

The public V4.1 adapter currently admits TP4/PP1, so reproducing the historical PP2 V4.1 numbers needs the PP2 x TP4 port (#1370) and a GGUF hybrid checkpoint. This generic PP test plan qualifies another admitted public model; it does not reproduce those historical numbers.

## Path coverage

| Path / provider | Format | Key conditions (shape, TP/EP, graph, capability) | Expected selection / fallback | Evidence (source / static / executed / measured) | Unverified scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V1 synchronous PP | Persistent request rows / histories | PP above one; fully empty step; opt-in | Retain live rows and matching scheduler record | Executed real scheduler and CPU InputBatch state tests; historical measurement | Current-main GPU serving, graphs and speed |
| Finished / preempted / resumed | Same | Removal during an empty step or later resumption | Remove stale records; resend resumed history | Executed CPU state and request lifecycle tests | GPU lifecycle |
| Disabled / nonempty | Same | OFF or any request scheduled | Original row replacement behavior on top of companion bugfix | Executed off/on CPU controls | GPU identity comparison |
| Unsupported explicit request | Other runner/state contracts | V2, async, external launcher, connectors, pooling, hybrid state or unsupported speculation | Construction refuses and names VLLM_PP_KEEP_BATCH | Executed capability/admission tests | No broader model qualification |
| Synchronous speculation | Step-owned draft snapshots | Multiple request groups; inherited bugfix | Apply each step's own proposals after its output | Executed real engine-loop cadence regression | Worker GPU production, transport and structured-output serving |

## Acceleration and benchmark contract (required for performance changes)

- Default enabled or opt-in: Opt-in via scheduler_config.pp_keep_batch or VLLM_PP_KEEP_BATCH=1; default off.
- Required CLI options and environment switches: V1, synchronous PP above one; admitted model/state contract. Errors name the requested setting.
- KV cache dtype used for the benchmark: Historical #1277 packed V4.1 KV; retention adds no codec.
- Wheel SHA or source commit: This branch: `main` `3c051b52e` plus #1371. The numbers below were measured on our build of the #1277 merge (`899e9ed33`) with the PP2 x TP4 port (#1370); this branch has not run on a GPU.
- PYTHONPATH, source overlays, or external native libraries used (write "none" if absent): No native library added by retention. The measurements used the V4.1 PP2 port (#1370), native kernels and a GGUF hybrid checkpoint that is not published.
- User-entry route-hit, speed, and output-quality evidence: MEASURED 2026-11-03 (table under Test Result): 32K/64K/128K round times 32.69/37.19/44.73 to 29.51/30.73/33.62 ms, same text and unchanged first-token time. The earlier aggregate included first-token timing; it is not the later decode-only contract. These values cannot be reproduced by this branch alone and do not qualify the repaired current-main port.
- Existing kernel/backend registry and capability-rejection reasons: No kernel priority change. Shared scheduler/runner admission rejects unsupported state contracts.
- Per-engine configuration and deprecated-variable compatibility: Typed serialized SchedulerConfig field, initialization-only alias, explicit typed override, no extra model graph hash salt.
- New/changed environment metadata and generated reference check: VLLM_PP_KEEP_BATCH registered as experimental; architecture/env references and all five gates pass.
- Route snapshot command and intentional changed rows (write "none" for refactors): python -m tools.sm70_route_snapshot --category moe --output /dev/stdout; none.
- SM70 registered variables / unregistered reads / model-parameter restrictions, before -> after: SM70 registrations unchanged; one generic PP alias added; no new unregistered execution reads; no expanded model admission.

## Test Result

**MEASURED, 2026-11-03,** 8x V100-SXM2-32GB, DeepSeek-V4.1 PP2 x TP4 (#1370), one request, DSpark 5, V1 runner, setting OFF -> ON, ms per verify round (aggregate including first-token time):

| prompt | OFF | ON | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32K | 32.69 | 29.51 | -9.7 % |
| 64K | 37.19 | 30.73 | -17.4 % |
| 128K | 44.73 | 33.62 | -24.8 % (84 -> 111 tok/s) |
| short, T=0 / T=1 | | | -0.17 / -0.30 ms |

Texts identical; first-token time unchanged. These were measured on the earlier code, before the correctness repairs now split out into #1371.

**Re-run on `main` for this PR, 2026-11-05,** CPU only (no visible GPU), branch = `3c051b52e` + #1371 + this commit:

- pytest, the ten files in the plan: 100 passed, 10 failed. The 10 failures are all in `tests/config/test_runtime_default_ownership.py` and fail identically on unmodified `main` (`SimpleNamespace` has no attribute `model`).
- `generate_env_reference --check`, `config_inventory --check`, `check_env_metadata.py`, `check_env_registration.py`, `generate_architecture_reference --check`: all pass. `check_layering.py` output is identical to `main`.
- ruff 0.14.0 `check` and `format --check` on the 16 changed Python files: pass.

Not run on this branch: any GPU or serving test, and no re-measurement of the table.

---
